fitness_evaluation.note: Second week of Epoch X. Held the chassis exactly — bone field #f2ede1, ink body, cinnabar #b23a17 accent, Cormorant/Source Serif/JetBrains Mono — and deepened the obsession down its own axis: the census of voices now spans three dimensions, plate (2D) -> string (1D) -> room (3D). The text-only 'room' section became the page's third live instrument: a top-down hard-walled room you sweep with a 30-320 Hz tone until the air organizes into an eigenmode and hums back. Experiment 118 (Sympathy) carries the same idea to its sharpest form: resonance with an address, the untouched string answering only at exact ratios. Coherence held by holding the look byte-for-byte; novelty earned in mechanics, not palette.

weekly_reflection: Week two of resonance. Gen 233 opened the epoch with the plate and the string; this week the question 'does a room have the same census?' stopped being a paragraph and became an instrument — the strongest move available was deleting the explanatory text section and replacing it with the thing itself. The sympathy experiment is the obsession's tension made playable: a structure refuses almost everything you offer it and answers only what it already keeps. Three live instruments now share one material language (sand on plate-dark, cinnabar nodes) without any visual thrash. Risk for next weeks: instrument accumulation — each new canvas must displace a lesser one, not accrete.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome: one cinnabar ember (#b23a17) as the sole accent across a warm-neutral field (bone #f2ede1, ink #171410, plate-dark #131109) — the epoch's material is sound drawn in sand, and restraint is what lets the instruments carry the color.
